You are designing an architecture change for the Rust project Callisto (repo at /tmp/callisto-relpr-debug, a worktree equivalent to orin-dx/callisto main). Read-only: do not edit files. Read the files named below yourself before designing.

## Problem
The composite action `.github/actions/callisto-action/scripts/create-or-update-release-pr.sh` maintains a long-lived "release PR" branch (`callisto/version-packages`) by: checking out current base (`main`), calling `callisto --format json release-pr decide --snapshot <json> ...` (Rust policy in `crates/callisto-model/src/release_pr.rs`, CLI in `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/release_pr.rs`), running `callisto version` (writes only Cargo.toml/package.json manifests, CHANGELOG.md, deletes .changeset/*.md), then `git switch -C <branch>; git add -A; git commit; git push --force-with-lease`, then `gh pr create/edit`. Before the push and before PR writes it re-collects the snapshot and runs `callisto release-pr verify --decision --snapshot` to detect races.

GitHub's automatic GITHUB_TOKEN cannot push (via git) content that changes `.github/workflows/*` on a ref. When `main`'s workflow files changed since the release branch was cut, the regenerated branch (current main + version bump) differs from the stale branch at that path, so the force push is rejected. Current mitigation: the snapshot records `workflowDeltaFromBase` per open PR (computed via `git diff origin/<branch>...HEAD -- .github/workflows`), and `ReleasePrDecisionV1::derive` returns `ReleasePrActionV1::Supersede { pull_request_number, expected_branch, replacement_branch: "<release_branch>--<base_sha>" }`: the action creates a new SHA-suffixed branch + new PR and closes the old PR. Users dislike the PR churn; a PAT with `workflows` scope is the documented opt-out but the maintainer refuses PATs.

## Discovery
changesets/action (the JS tool this mirrors) does NOT use `git push` by default. It uses `@changesets/ghcommit` `commitChangesSinceBase(..., base: {commit: <main sha>}, force: true)` which (see its core.ts "FORCE UPDATE" path): (1) creates/force-updates a temporary branch `changesets-ghcommit-temp/<branch>` at the base sha via REST `git.createRef`/`git.updateRef`, (2) calls GraphQL `createCommitOnBranch` on the temp branch with `expectedHeadOid = base sha` and `fileChanges { additions:[{path, contents(base64)}], deletions:[{path}] }` containing only the generated files, (3) REST `git.updateRef(force: true)` moves the real branch to the new commit sha, (4) deletes the temp branch. Comment in their code: "We cannot reset the branch and then commit because if the branch has an existing PR, GitHub will auto-close as it sees there's no changes with the base." This never *creates* workflow-file content with the token (the new commit's parent is main, whose workflows are current; the ref move points at an existing commit), which is why changesets updates its PR in place indefinitely without a PAT. Bonus: API commits are GitHub-signed ("Verified") and attributed to github-actions[bot].

We have NOT empirically confirmed in GitHub Actions that (a) raw `git push` of the regenerated branch is actually rejected, or (b) the temp-branch + createCommitOnBranch + updateRef(force) flow succeeds with the default GITHUB_TOKEN when workflows diverged. The plan must start with a falsifiable spike (Phase 0) with GO/NO-GO criteria.

## Architectural constraints (read these files)
- `.claude/specs/SPEC-RELEASE-PR-DECISION-014.json` (draft): Callisto owns policy (credential-free, read-only `decide`); the shell action is a thin executor that gathers a credential-free snapshot, branches only on the closed decision kind, and rechecks expected PR/branch facts immediately before each forge mutation. AC-002..AC-005 encode create/update/supersede, SHA-suffixed replacement, schema-versioned outputs.
- `.claude/specs/SPEC-RELEASE-INTERFACES-013.json` AC (around line 40) encodes the SHA-suffixed supersede fallback contract and "recomputes rather than rebasing" and "requires no elevated token".
- `docs/06-publishing.md` paragraph "Repository durable-release workflow" documents supersede + optional PAT.
- `crates/callisto-model/src/release_pr.rs` (types: ReleasePrConfigV1, ReleasePrSnapshotV1 {schemaVersion:1, deny_unknown_fields, openPullRequests[{number, headRepository, headBranch, workflowDeltaFromBase}]}, ReleasePrActionV1 {Noop|Create|Update|Supersede}, ReleasePrDecisionV1, derive(), verify_snapshot(), managed_branch_shape() accepting canonical or canonical--<40hex>).
- `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/release_pr.rs`, `crates/callisto-cli/src/cli.rs` (ReleasePrArgs: Decide, Verify; global `--format json`, `--cwd`).
- `.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml`, `.github/actions/callisto-action/scripts/create-or-update-release-pr.sh`, tests `.github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_contract.sh` (stubs callisto/gh/git as bash functions) and `test_release_pr_decide_binary_contract.sh` (runs the real binary and checks the script's jq expressions), `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml` (version-pr job: permissions contents:write, pull-requests:write; checkout persist-credentials:true).
- Layer rule: `callisto-model` is Layer 1 (permissive license, no AGPL deps, no I/O of forge credentials). `callisto-vcs` runs git through a `CommandRunner`; `callisto-cli` has `CliCommandRunner`.
- CLAUDE.md: safe Rust only, atomic writes, no emojis in docs; validate each fix individually; tests must exercise real binaries where the contract crosses the Rust->shell boundary (a prior bug shipped because the stub test hand-wrote camelCase JSON).
- Live state: PR #48 is currently open on branch `callisto/version-packages--567f321c8cae20c66ab7bf90ca59d493978c84b0` (a retained SHA-suffixed replacement). After this change, the next run should UPDATE #48 in place; existing `--sha` branches must remain accepted as managed.

## Design questions to resolve (give a recommendation with rationale for each)
1. Where should the createCommitOnBranch payload be built: (A) bash+jq in the executor from `git status --porcelain`/`git diff --name-status <base>` + base64 file contents, or (B) a new credential-free Rust command `callisto release-pr commit-plan --base-commit <sha> [--message]` emitting a typed `ReleasePrCommitPlanV1 { schemaVersion, baseCommit, message, additions:[{path, contentsBase64}], deletions:[{path}] }` that the shell forwards to `gh api graphql`. Consider testability (unit tests in Rust vs. bash), path/encoding edge cases (deleted changesets, renamed files, CRLF, binary, large CHANGELOGs, symlinks/executable bits which createCommitOnBranch cannot express), and the spec's "no policy in shell" rule.
2. Exact executor sequence with race safety: snapshot -> decide -> `callisto version` -> commit-plan -> verify -> temp branch create/force-update at base sha (REST or GraphQL) -> createCommitOnBranch(expectedHeadOid=base) -> verify again -> updateRef(force) real branch -> verify -> PR create/edit -> temp branch cleanup (also on failure). `updateRef` has no compare-and-swap; propose adding `headSha` of each open PR to the snapshot so `verify` can detect a moved head before the force move. Should the temp branch name be deterministic (e.g. `callisto/version-packages--staging`) and must `managed_branch_shape` reject/ignore it?
3. Model changes: remove `workflow_delta_from_base` and `Supersede` (schema bump snapshot v2 / decision v2?) vs keep `Supersede` reserved as an optional fallback if the API path is rejected at runtime (executor could fall back to supersede on a 403?). Recommend one; consider `#[non_exhaustive]`, `deny_unknown_fields`, the `Wire` schema-version check pattern, and that the CLI and action ship from the same commit.
4. Phase 0 spike design: how to empirically test in real GitHub Actions with the default token, cheaply and safely (scratch repo vs a `workflow_dispatch` workflow on this repo), what exact cases to run (raw git push regenerated branch; temp-branch+createCommitOnBranch+updateRef; also direct `git push origin <main sha>:refs/heads/<branch>` as a cheaper git-only alternative), and GO/NO-GO criteria.
5. Which artifacts must change: specs 014 and 013 (which ACs, revision notes), PLAN-014 or a new PLAN-015, docs (06-publishing.md, ARCHITECTURE.md §12?, README), action inputs (`setup_git_user` becomes vestigial), tests (stub contract test, real-binary contract test, Rust unit tests, trycmd help snapshots), changeset entry.
6. Risks/edge cases: GraphQL payload size limits; PR auto-close if branch momentarily equals base; the `release-candidate` job's `.commit.verification.verified` check on the merge commit; branch protection/rulesets on the managed branch; forks; `gh` availability; behavior when temp branch cleanup fails; idempotent re-run when nothing changed.

Deliver: a concrete, ordered implementation plan (phases and tasks with file paths, function names, and test names), your recommendation for each question, and a short list of open questions only the maintainer can answer.

- courier:changeset: Trigger when the user asks to add a changeset or document a change: "add a changeset", "document this change", "what changed here". Extracts the consumer-facing meaning of a diff: classifies consumer_impact (behavior-change, new-capability, internal-only) and semver_impact (major, minor, patch, none) per shared/references/changesets.md's decision table, then writes a summary scaled to that classification. A diff spanning multiple independent topics — common on a backlog/catch-up run, not just a single PR — produces one changeset per topic, not one bundled entry. When the change came via smith, pass along implementer's criteria_evidence — changeset-analyzer uses those exact locations instead of reconstructing approximate ones from the diff.
- courier:commit: Trigger when the user asks to commit code or write a commit message: "commit this", "write a commit message", "commit the staged changes". Reads the staged git diff and produces a conventional commit message explaining why the change was made, not what changed — the diff already shows what changed.
- courier:post-review: Trigger when the user has an already-drafted review or reply and wants it posted: "post this review", "reply to this comment", "mark this thread resolved", "submit my review comments". Takes drafted content — from the built-in `code-review` skill's findings, from `courier/receive-feedback`'s response plan, or typed directly by the user — and posts it to GitHub via `gh pr review` or `gh pr comment`. Does not draft content itself; this skill is purely mechanical execution of something already written, gated by explicit user confirmation before any post fires.
- courier:pr: Trigger when the user asks to open a PR or write a PR description: "open a PR", "create a pull request", "write the PR description". Given a diff, a linked spec, and a linked requirement, produces a PR title and body a reviewer with zero context can act on, then opens the PR via `gh pr create` after user confirmation.
- courier:receive-feedback: Trigger when the user asks to process or triage incoming review feedback: "address the feedback", "respond to review comments", "what do these comments mean", "triage this review". Assembles a review package — diff summary, linked spec, test results, open questions — so the author has full context to respond without re-reading the whole thread. Does not categorize individual comments by priority; that's the caller's judgment call, made with `shared/references/github.md`'s vocabulary in hand. This is for feedback received on the user's own PR — critiquing someone else's PR is the built-in `code-review` skill's job, not this one.
- courier:release: Trigger when the user asks to cut a release or summarize what's in one: "cut a release", "what's in this release", "generate release notes". Aggregates changeset@2 entries since the last release into a release-artifact@2: filters consumer_impact: internal-only entries, computes the version as max(semver_impact) across the rest applied to the prior version, and carries each changeset's summary through unedited.
- muse:component: Trigger when the user asks to spec a UI component: "spec this component", "draft a component spec", "write a spec for this design", "audit this component spec", "is this component spec ready?", "gate this component spec". Given a requirement@1 or free-text design intent, produces a spec@1 covering props, variants, per-state observable behavior, and accessibility criteria as testable propositions. Every criterion is falsifiable from outside the implementation; error cases and invalid prop combinations carry is_error_case: true. No TBDs anywhere in the document — genuinely unknown items go in non_goals or the reasoning scratchpad instead. Gated by a binding exit gate before the spec proceeds to planning.
- navigator:plan: Trigger this skill when the user says "write a plan for X", "how do we implement this spec", "break this down into tasks", "what are the implementation steps", "create an implementation plan", or "plan this out". Also activate when a spec (spec@1) exists and the user is ready to move to implementation but hasn't broken it down yet. Produces a plan@1 artifact where every task includes exact file paths, a brief implementation approach, exact implementation code, the exact tests proving each criterion, a conventional commit message, and covers_criteria linking the task to specific acceptance criteria. spec_file_path and linked_requirement are propagated from the source spec. No TBDs. No "implement as appropriate." Every step is mechanically executable by a developer with zero domain context.
- ranger:audit: Trigger this skill when the user asks to perform a bug hunt, code audit, find bugs, security audit, defect scan, vulnerability scan, code review for bugs, or asks "what's wrong with this code." Activate for any codebase language — Rust, TypeScript, or JavaScript. 5-phase pipeline: (1) recon builds a verified module manifest and detects the primary language; (2) scanner reads language-specific hazard taxonomies and emits candidates in live files only; (3) boundary-tracer (conditional) traces field survival for T7/T10 candidates; (4) adversary refutes each candidate by tracing control flow — unrebutted candidates survive as confirmed (concrete failing scenario stated) or plausible (no refutation, but reachability depends on state outside the code); (5) exit-gate re-reads code from scratch, verifies confirmed findings are resolved, checks sibling gaps, confirms compile/tests pass, carries plausible findings forward for human review without blocking on them, and escalates after 3 failed retries. Never reports bugs in dead or unreachable code. Output follows finding-report@1.
- scribe:architect: Trigger when ranger has returned a finding-report@1 and the confirmed defect class needs a structural fix — a change to the architecture, type system, interface boundary, or abstraction layer — rather than patches to individual instances. Given a finding-report@1, produces a spec@1 for the structural change that makes the defect class impossible or unrepresentable, not merely documented or harder to introduce. Acceptance criteria must be falsifiable at the type or API level.
- scribe:audit-architecture: Trigger when a draft spec@1 needs checking against the workspace's whole-system architecture — not another spec, and not a single signature — before it reaches scribe/gate-spec: "check this spec against our architecture", "does this fit the system", "audit this against the arch model". Given a spec@1, checks it against the persisted arch-model@1 for boundary violations, competing abstractions, and invariant conflicts, building or refreshing the model first if it's absent or stale for the area the spec touches. Returns specific, rewritten fixes on fail, the same standard as scribe/audit-spec but at system scope instead of spec scope.
- scribe:audit-spec: Trigger when the user asks to review a spec's quality: "review this spec", "is this spec complete?", "audit this spec". Given a spec@1, adversarially reviews it for untestable criteria, ambiguous language, missing error cases, scope overlap with other specs, and incomplete sections. Returns a structured issue list with specific rewritten suggested fixes, not generic guidance. Named audit-spec rather than audit because the bare word audit is already ranger's plugin-level skill name (code/bug auditing) — a different domain entirely.
- scribe:correct-spec: Trigger when implementer reports that a spec criterion contradicts what the system actually does: a spec_contradiction status from smith. Given a spec_file_path, the criterion_id of the affected acceptance criterion, and a contradiction report (what the spec says vs. what the system actually does), revises the affected criterion — and any criteria that depend on it — and returns a corrected spec@1 with revision_note set. Use this when implementation reveals the spec itself is wrong, not merely hard to satisfy.
- scribe:draft-spec: Trigger when the user asks to write or draft a spec: "spec this out", "draft a spec", "write a spec for this requirement". Given a requirement@1 and optionally a research-report@1, produces a spec@1 draft with purpose, scope, non_goals, api_surface (if applicable), and acceptance criteria. Every criterion is a testable proposition; error cases carry is_error_case: true. No TBDs anywhere in the document — genuinely unknown items go in non_goals or the reasoning scratchpad instead.
- scribe:gate-spec: Trigger when a spec@1 needs a definitive pass/fail judgment before it enters planning: "gate this spec", "is this spec ready?", "check this spec before we plan it". Default disposition is fail — the spec must earn a pass. Passes only if every acceptance criterion is testable with no vague language, no TBDs remain, error cases are explicitly covered, and scope is narrow enough for one planning cycle. This gate checks the spec on its own terms — whole-system architectural fit is scribe/audit-architecture's job upstream, not re-litigated here. On fail, returns blockers specific enough for scribe/draft-spec to act on without further clarification.
- scribe:spec-drift: Trigger when the user asks whether implemented code still matches its spec, weeks or months after implementation: "check spec drift", "does the code still match this spec?", "has this spec drifted?". Given a spec@1 (via spec_file_path) and a workspace root, reads the spec from disk and the implementation from the workspace, and reports each criterion as covered (implemented and tested), uncovered (no matching implementation), or drifted (implementation exists but diverges from the criterion's contract). This is an on-demand diagnostic, not a blocking gate — scribe/gate-spec is the blocking gate.
- scribe:verify-spec: Trigger when the user asks whether a spec matches its source: "is this grounded?", "does this spec match the requirement?", "check this spec against the requirement". Given a draft spec@1 plus the originating requirement@1 and optional research-report@1, checks whether each acceptance criterion is grounded in the source artifacts. Classifies criteria as supported, unsupported, or overfitted. Collects evidence only — does not produce a pass/fail verdict. Use before implementation, not after — for post-implementation drift, use scribe/spec-drift instead.
- sentinel:gate: Trigger this skill when the user says "verify this", "check this spec", "check this plan", "check this requirement", "check this PR", "is this done?", "review this for completeness", "does this meet the criteria?", "gate this", or "quality check" — also before stage transitions: starting implementation from a spec, shipping from an implementation, opening a PR from a branch. Applies to any stage artifact: requirements, specs, plans, implementations, PRs. Do not activate for general Q&A, code explanation, or exploratory work with no artifact boundary being crossed. The gate either clears the artifact for the next stage or returns specific, actionable blockers to the producing agent.
- smith:implement: Activate when the user says "implement this", "execute the plan", "write the code", "build this feature", "generate tests for X", "write tests for this spec", "refactor this without changing behavior", or "explain what this code does" — also when handed a plan@1 to execute, or a spec@1 exists but no plan. Every task: design the approach, write the implementation and comprehensive tests proving the covers_criteria, confirm the full suite passes, commit. Mutation testing then verifies the test suite would catch real faults — not a write-test-first ordering — surviving mutants return to the implementer as precision tests before the exit gate runs. The sentinel exit gate verifies all spec criteria independently at the end, reading the codebase from scratch and assuming the implementation is incomplete. Works from plan@1 (preferred) or spec@1 directly.
- vanguard:research: Activate when the user says "I need to understand X before deciding", "is there a way to do Y", "what are the options for Z", "research this", "investigate this", "what does the codebase already do for X", "prior art on Y", or "what are the risks of approach Z" — also when the approach for a spec or plan is unclear, when checking what dependencies exist for a feature, or when any design question needs an evidence base before commitment. Investigates the question across internal sources (specs, docs, codebase patterns, manifests) and external sources as needed, then produces a research-report@1 that distinguishes confirmed findings from likely inferences from unverified assumptions, with a falsifiable recommendation and explicit confidence level so a spec writer (scribe) isn't surprised by implementation reality.
- weaver:audit-backlog: Trigger when the user asks about overall backlog health: "what's in the backlog", "audit the backlog", "what requirements are missing coverage". Cross-references all open requirement@1 objects against existing specs and implementation files. Returns per-requirement status (covered, partial, missing, duplicate) with evidence, plus a structured summary — per-status counts and an optional one-clause note, not a prose paragraph. Named audit-backlog rather than bare audit because that word is already ranger's plugin-level skill name (code/bug auditing) — a different domain entirely.
- weaver:capture-need: Trigger when the user describes a raw need in free text: "we need X", "the problem is Y", "users are asking for Z". Converts unstructured text into a structured requirement@1 draft — id, statement, stakeholder, why, done_when — without asking clarifying questions. Fields that cannot be inferred are omitted, not fabricated. out_of_scope is intentionally left empty for weaver/connect-requirement or a human to fill in.
- weaver:clarify-requirement: Trigger when a requirement@1 draft from weaver/capture-need has gaps to close before a spec can be written: "is this requirement complete?", "what's missing from this requirement". Given a requirement@1, evaluates gaps in priority order — testability of done_when, specificity of stakeholder, explicitness of out_of_scope — and either asks one focused question or returns the completed requirement with out_of_scope populated. One question per invocation, never a list.
- weaver:connect-requirement: Trigger when the user asks whether a specific requirement already exists or relates to other work: "is this already captured?", "does this overlap with an existing requirement?", "what does this relate to?". Given one requirement@1 (or a small named set), searches the workspace for related specs and implementation files, and checks for duplicate or overlapping requirements. Returns coverage status and duplicate_of references scoped to just the requirement(s) given — not a full backlog sweep.
- weaver:prioritize-backlog: Trigger when the user asks what to work on first from a set of requirements: "what should we prioritize", "rank the backlog", "what's most urgent". Given a list of requirement@1 drafts, ranks them by impact, urgency, and dependency order — a requirement another depends on ranks above the one depending on it, even if its own impact/urgency score is lower. Returns an ordered list with a concrete rationale per requirement.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Executes a typed Callisto release-PR decision. Forge reads stay here; all
# create/update/supersede policy belongs to `callisto release-pr decide`.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$INPUT_CWD"

# This checkout starts on the configured base. Preserve its exact commit for
# both observations; after `version` commits, HEAD intentionally changes.
base_commit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

release_pr_snapshot() {
  local raw_prs initial enriched number repository branch workflow_delta
  raw_prs=$(gh pr list --state open --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --limit 1000 --json number,headRefName,headRepository)
  initial=$(jq -c '[.[] | {
    number,
    headRepository: (.headRepository.nameWithOwner // ""),
    headBranch: .headRefName,
    workflowDeltaFromBase: false
  }]' <<< "$raw_prs")
  enriched='[]'

  # This is forge/Git observation, not policy: fetch every safe same-repository
  # PR branch and report whether its workflow files differ from the checked-out
  # base. Callisto decides whether that fact requires a replacement PR.
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r number repository branch; do
    workflow_delta=false
    if [[ "$repository" == "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" ]] && git check-ref-format --branch "$branch" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
      git fetch --no-tags origin "refs/heads/$branch:refs/remotes/origin/$branch"
      if ! git diff --quiet "refs/remotes/origin/$branch...HEAD" -- .github/workflows; then
        workflow_delta=true
      fi
    fi
    enriched=$(jq -c \
      --argjson number "$number" \
      --arg repository "$repository" \
      --arg branch "$branch" \
      --argjson workflow_delta "$workflow_delta" \
      '. + [{number: $number, headRepository: $repository, headBranch: $branch, workflowDeltaFromBase: $workflow_delta}]' \
      <<< "$enriched")
  done < <(jq -r '.[] | [.number, .headRepository, .headBranch] | @tsv' <<< "$initial")

  jq -cn \
    --arg repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
    --arg base_branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" \
    --arg base_commit "$base_commit" \
    --argjson open_pull_requests "$enriched" \
    '{schemaVersion: 1, repository: $repository, baseBranch: $base_branch, baseCommit: $base_commit, openPullRequests: $open_pull_requests}'
}

snapshot=$(release_pr_snapshot)
decision=$(callisto --format json release-pr decide \
  --snapshot "$snapshot" \
  --repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
  --base-branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" \
  --release-branch "$INPUT_RELEASE_BRANCH")
decision_kind=$(jq -r '.action.kind' <<< "$decision")

case "$decision_kind" in
  noop)
    echo 'hasChangesets=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    matrix=$(callisto matrix --format json | jq -c '[.platformTargets[].targets[]] | unique_by(.artifactName)')
    echo "nativeMatrix=$matrix" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo '::notice::No changesets. This action does not publish, tag, download artifacts, or create releases; use the durable repository workflow.'
    exit 0
    ;;
  create)
    release_branch=$(jq -r '.action.branch' <<< "$decision")
    existing_pr=''
    ;;
  update)
    existing_pr=$(jq -r '.action.pullRequestNumber' <<< "$decision")
    release_branch=$(jq -r '.action.branch' <<< "$decision")
    ;;
  supersede)
    existing_pr=$(jq -r '.action.pullRequestNumber' <<< "$decision")
    release_branch=$(jq -r '.action.replacementBranch' <<< "$decision")
    ;;
  *) echo "::error::Callisto returned unsupported release PR decision kind: $decision_kind"; exit 1 ;;
esac

echo 'hasChangesets=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
if [[ -n "$existing_pr" ]]; then
  existing_body=$(gh pr view "$existing_pr" --json body --jq '.body')
  body=$(printf '%s' "$existing_body" | callisto compose-pr-body --existing-body - --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
else
  body=$(callisto compose-pr-body --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
fi

read -ra command <<< "$INPUT_VERSION_COMMAND"
"${command[@]}"
test -n "$(git status --porcelain)" || { echo '::error::pending changesets produced no release-PR delta'; exit 1; }
if [[ "$INPUT_SETUP_GIT_USER" == true ]]; then
  git config user.name 'github-actions[bot]'
  git config user.email '41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com'
fi
git switch -C "$release_branch"
git add -A
git commit -m "$INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE"

# A local commit does not authorize a stale force-push. Re-observe immediately
# before mutating the remote branch, then again before GitHub label/PR writes.
current_snapshot=$(release_pr_snapshot)
callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$current_snapshot" > /dev/null
git push --force-with-lease origin "$release_branch"

current_snapshot=$(release_pr_snapshot)
callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$current_snapshot" > /dev/null

label_exists=$(gh label list --limit 1000 --json name --jq 'any(.[]; .name == env.INPUT_PR_LABEL)')
if [[ "$label_exists" != true ]]; then
  gh label create "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --color 0e8a16 --description 'Callisto release packages'
fi

case "$decision_kind" in
  create)
    gh pr create --head "$release_branch" --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$body" --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL"
    ;;
  update)
    gh pr edit "$existing_pr" --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$body" --add-label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL"
    ;;
  supersede)
    new_pr_url=$(gh pr create --head "$release_branch" --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$body" --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL")
    gh pr close "$existing_pr" --comment "Superseded by $new_pr_url because GitHub requires elevated workflow authority to update this generated branch. The replacement was recomputed from the current base branch and pending changesets."
    ;;
esac

on:

  workflow_dispatch:

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: durable-release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify release candidate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Build local Callisto
        uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local

      - name: Install just
        uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4.0.0
        with:
          just-version: '1.58.0'

      - name: Format Check
        run: just fmt-check

      - name: Clippy Lints
        run: just lint

      - name: Install release verification tools
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@0758d235715de2f3551eacc980d9ae8fce9342c3 # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest,ripgrep

      - name: Unit & Integration Tests
        run: just test

      - name: WASM Target Check
        run: just wasm-check

      - name: Install cargo-deny
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@0758d235715de2f3551eacc980d9ae8fce9342c3 # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny

      - name: Supply Chain Audit
        run: just audit

      - name: Reject mutable GitHub Actions references
        run: .github/tests/verify-action-pins.sh

  version-pr:
    name: Create or update the Callisto release PR
    needs: verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    outputs:
      has_pending_changesets: ${{ steps.version-pr.outputs.hasChangesets }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: true # zizmor: ignore[artipacked] this isolated version-PR job must authenticate its managed-branch push; no artifacts are uploaded from it.
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - name: Compose, version, and open the release PR
        id: version-pr
        uses: $/.github/actions/callisto-action
        with:
          setup_callisto: 'false'
          branch: main
          release_branch: callisto/version-packages
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

  release-candidate:
    name: Identify a merged Callisto release PR
    needs: [verify, version-pr]
    if: needs.version-pr.outputs.has_pending_changesets == 'false'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      is_release_pr: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.is_release_pr }}
    steps:
      - id: candidate
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # This only schedules the job. `release plan` verifies the actual
          # parent-to-merge delta; labels and PR metadata are never authority.
          # The GitHub API check is complementary provenance evidence: a
          # trusted merge must be both an actual merge of the managed PR and
          # a GitHub-verified signed commit. It cannot be a direct push.
          prs=$(gh api --paginate "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${GITHUB_SHA}/pulls" --jq '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == "main" and (.head.ref == "callisto/version-packages" or (.head.ref | test("^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$"))))] | length')
          verified=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${GITHUB_SHA}" --jq '.commit.verification.verified')
          if [[ "$prs" == 1 && "$verified" == true ]]; then
            echo 'is_release_pr=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'is_release_pr=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  plan:
    name: Derive ephemeral intent from the merged release commit
    needs: release-candidate
    if: needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - name: Derive and hash intent
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          callisto release plan --from-release-commit "$GITHUB_SHA" --out release-intent.json
          shasum -a 256 release-intent.json > release-intent.json.sha256
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: |
            release-intent.json
            release-intent.json.sha256
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

    name: Build the intent-bound source tree
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      attestations: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4.0.0
        with:
          just-version: '1.58.0'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: .release-handoff
      - name: Verify handoff and build
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          (cd .release-handoff && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          callisto release inspect --input .release-handoff/release-intent.json
          mkdir -p release-artifacts
          just build
      - name: Attest declared binary artifacts
        if: hashFiles('release-artifacts/**') != ''
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-path: release-artifacts/**
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: |
            .release-handoff
            release-artifacts
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  environment-policy:
    name: Verify release Environment protection
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Require release Environment reviewers
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          reviewers=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/environments/release" --jq '.protection_rules // [] | map(select(.type == "required_reviewers")) | length')
          [[ "$reviewers" != 0 ]] || { echo '::error::GitHub Environment release has no required-reviewers protection rule'; exit 1; }

  execute:
    name: Execute approved release
    needs: environment-policy
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: release
    permissions:
      contents: write
      attestations: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: .release-intent
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: .release-build
      - name: Verify same-run handoff before credentials
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          (cd .release-intent && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          cmp .release-intent/release-intent.json .release-build/release-intent.json
      - name: Execute verified release
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
          TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TWINE_PASSWORD }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          state_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-state/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          mkdir -p "$state_dir"
          args=(--intent .release-intent/release-intent.json --state "$state_dir/execution-state.json")
          if [[ -f .release-build/release-artifacts/manifest.json ]]; then
            args+=(--artifact-manifest .release-build/release-artifacts/manifest.json --artifact-dir .release-build/release-artifacts)
          fi
          callisto release execute "${args[@]}"

# Callisto Codebase Guide for Claude & AI Agents

This repository follows the centralized AI agent guidelines documented in [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md).

---

## Quick Reference

### Primary Task Runner Commands
- `just` / `just ci-fast` (default): Full verification suite minus `coverage`. Use this for everyday pre-PR checks.
- `just ci`: Same, plus `coverage`. Matches CI parity; slow (coverage recompiles the whole workspace under instrumentation).
- `just test` / `moon run :test`: Run all unit, integration, doctests, and E2E lifecycle test suites.
- `just lint` / `moon run :lint`: Run Clippy lints with `-D warnings`.
- `just fmt` / `moon run :format`: Format code automatically.

### Key Architectural Invariants
1. **Safe Rust Only**: `unsafe_code = "forbid"` across all crates.
2. **Format Preservation**: Manifest modifications use CST editors (`toml_edit`, `serde_json` indentation fingerprinting).
3. **Atomic File Persistence**: File edits use `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write`.
4. **Layer Isolation**: Layer 1 crates (`callisto-model`, `callisto-format`) must remain permissive (`MIT OR Apache-2.0`) and never depend on AGPL crates.
5. **No Emojis in Documentation**: Keep docs clean, technical, scannable, and emoji-free.

### Build/test scoping
Full pipeline: `just ci`/`just test`/`just lint`. For scoped iteration, one direct `cargo test -p <crate>` / `cargo clippy -p <crate>` invocation -- not `moon run <project>:test`, whose per-project fan-out serializes on `target/`'s build lock (see `Justfile`'s `lint` comment; `moon`'s own `test`/`lint` tasks are literally `cargo test -p $project` / `cargo clippy -p $project` each).

### `Cargo.lock`
Never `git checkout -- Cargo.lock` as pre-commit cleanup -- thrashes the build cache, can turn `just ci` into a multi-hour run. A diff means investigate, not discard.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# test_release_pr_contract.sh stubs `callisto` with hand-written camelCase
# JSON fixtures, so it only proves the script's control flow given already
# correctly-shaped input -- it structurally cannot catch a mismatch between
# what the real binary serializes and what this script's `jq` expects. That
# gap is exactly how a snake_case regression in ReleasePrActionV1 (fields
# inside a #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase", tag = "kind")] enum are NOT
# renamed by rename_all -- only the tag is) shipped to production and broke
# every release run past the first (`gh pr view null`, from `jq -r
# '.action.pullRequestNumber'` reading a field that didn't exist).
#
# This test compiles and calls the real `callisto` binary and asserts the
# exact `jq` expressions this action's script uses against its real output.
set -euo pipefail

action_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
workspace_root="$(cd "$action_dir/../../.." && pwd)"

cargo build -p callisto-cli --quiet --manifest-path "$workspace_root/Cargo.toml"
callisto_bin="$workspace_root/target/debug/callisto"

fail=0

assert_jq_matches_real_output() {
  local label="$1" workflow_delta="$2" expect_kind="$3"
  local snapshot decision decision_kind existing_pr

  snapshot=$(jq -cn \
    --arg repository 'orin-dx/callisto' \
    --arg base_branch main \
    --arg base_commit '0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567' \
    --argjson workflow_delta "$workflow_delta" \
    '{schemaVersion: 1, repository: $repository, baseBranch: $base_branch, baseCommit: $base_commit,
      openPullRequests: [{number: 42, headRepository: $repository, headBranch: "callisto/version-packages",
      workflowDeltaFromBase: $workflow_delta}]}')

  decision=$("$callisto_bin" --format json release-pr decide \
    --snapshot "$snapshot" --repository orin-dx/callisto --base-branch main \
    --release-branch callisto/version-packages --cwd "$workspace_root")

  # These are the exact expressions create-or-update-release-pr.sh evaluates.
  decision_kind=$(jq -r '.action.kind' <<< "$decision")
  existing_pr=$(jq -r '.action.pullRequestNumber' <<< "$decision")

  if [[ "$decision_kind" != "$expect_kind" ]]; then
    echo "FAIL ($label): expected decision kind '$expect_kind', got '$decision_kind': $decision"
    fail=1
    return
  fi
  if [[ "$existing_pr" != "42" ]]; then
    echo "FAIL ($label): jq -r '.action.pullRequestNumber' resolved to '$existing_pr' instead of 42 -- this is exactly what made the script run \`gh pr view null\`: $decision"
    fail=1
    return
  fi
  echo "PASS ($label): real binary output round-trips through the script's jq expressions"
}

# has_pending_changesets must be true against this workspace for either case
# below to produce anything but a noop -- true as long as a changeset file
# is pending, which this repository's own release process requires anyway.
shopt -s nullglob
changesets=("$workspace_root"/.changeset/*.md)
shopt -u nullglob
if [[ ${#changesets[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo 'SKIP: no pending changesets in this checkout; cannot exercise update/supersede decisions'
  exit 0
fi

assert_jq_matches_real_output 'update (no workflow delta)' false update
assert_jq_matches_real_output 'supersede (workflow delta)' true supersede

exit "$fail"

3	This document covers authentication setup for registry publishing, with particular attention
4	to npm, where there are two distinct auth patterns and common points of confusion.
5	
6	---
7	
8	## Repository durable-release workflow
9	
10	Callisto's own `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml` separates release work into four
11	authority boundaries. A push with pending changesets creates or updates the release PR. That
12	PR versions manifests and changelogs and removes only the changesets it consumed. Nothing is
13	removed from `main` until that PR is merged.
14	
15	The normal GitHub flow keeps one `callisto/version-packages` release PR and recomputes it from
16	the current base branch whenever changesets land. This is a reconstruction from `main`, not a
17	literal rebase of an old generated commit: recomputation prevents stale version, changelog, or
18	changeset-deletion edits from being carried forward. GitHub's built-in workflow token can refuse
19	to force-update that long-lived branch after `main` has changed a workflow. In that uncommon
20	case Callisto automatically creates a SHA-suffixed replacement branch and release PR from the
21	same current `main` and changesets, then closes the superseded PR with a link. No publishing
22	credential or elevated GitHub token is required; subsequent ordinary updates continue on the
23	replacement PR. Repositories that require the same PR number through that GitHub-specific edge
24	case may optionally provide an App or fine-grained token with workflow-write authority to both
25	checkout and `callisto-action`'s `github_token` input.
26	
27	After a merge, the workflow derives a transient release intent from the signed merge commit's
28	actual delta, builds from that exact commit, and passes the intent between jobs as a same-run
29	GitHub artifact with a SHA-256 sidecar. It is not committed and it is never recovered from a
30	cache. The execute job rechecks the handoff before calling `callisto release execute`.
31	
32	Create a GitHub Environment named `release` before enabling registry credentials. Configure
33	at least one required reviewer and appropriate branch/tag deployment rules in the repository's
34	Environment settings. The workflow queries the Environment API and fails if the reviewer rule
35	is absent; the `environment: release` job boundary is what prevents registry secrets from being
36	available to planning or build jobs.
37	
38	An administrator must also enable a branch-protection rule or ruleset on `main` that requires

# Publishing with Callisto

This document covers authentication setup for registry publishing, with particular attention
to npm, where there are two distinct auth patterns and common points of confusion.

---

## Repository durable-release workflow

Callisto's own `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml` separates release work into four
authority boundaries. A push with pending changesets creates or updates the release PR. That
PR versions manifests and changelogs and removes only the changesets it consumed. Nothing is
removed from `main` until that PR is merged.

The normal GitHub flow keeps one `callisto/version-packages` release PR and recomputes it from
the current base branch whenever changesets land. This is a reconstruction from `main`, not a
literal rebase of an old generated commit: recomputation prevents stale version, changelog, or
changeset-deletion edits from being carried forward. GitHub's built-in workflow token can refuse
to force-update that long-lived branch after `main` has changed a workflow. In that uncommon
case Callisto automatically creates a SHA-suffixed replacement branch and release PR from the
same current `main` and changesets, then closes the superseded PR with a link. No publishing
credential or elevated GitHub token is required; subsequent ordinary updates continue on the
replacement PR. Repositories that require the same PR number through that GitHub-specific edge
case may optionally provide an App or fine-grained token with workflow-write authority to both
checkout and `callisto-action`'s `github_token` input.

After a merge, the workflow derives a transient release intent from the signed merge commit's
actual delta, builds from that exact commit, and passes the intent between jobs as a same-run
GitHub artifact with a SHA-256 sidecar. It is not committed and it is never recovered from a
cache. The execute job rechecks the handoff before calling `callisto release execute`.

Create a GitHub Environment named `release` before enabling registry credentials. Configure
at least one required reviewer and appropriate branch/tag deployment rules in the repository's
Environment settings. The workflow queries the Environment API and fails if the reviewer rule
is absent; the `environment: release` job boundary is what prevents registry secrets from being
available to planning or build jobs.

An administrator must also enable a branch-protection rule or ruleset on `main` that requires
CODEOWNERS review. [`.github/CODEOWNERS`](../.github/CODEOWNERS) names the real owner for
workflow and action changes, but GitHub does not enforce review merely because that file exists.

Only the `execute` job may receive `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, or `TWINE_PASSWORD`.
Do not put those secrets at workflow scope, in build jobs, or in an action input. Binary releases
add exact files plus `release-artifacts/manifest.json` to the build handoff; their GitHub build
attestations are verified by Callisto before upload. Source-only releases do not need that
manifest.

`callisto-action` is now a compatibility version-PR action only. Its former `publish` and
`create_github_release` inputs are ignored; it never publishes, tags, downloads artifacts, or
creates a forge release. The repository durable workflow is the supported release path.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Verify permissions that GitHub only enforces when a guarded release path is
# actually exercised. Keeping this separate from the generic action-pin check
# makes the release authority contract visible and testable on every PR.
set -euo pipefail

workflow=.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml

job_block() {
  local job="$1" next_job="$2"
  sed -n "/^  ${job}:$/,/^  ${next_job}:$/p" "$workflow"
}

require_line() {
  local block="$1" expected="$2" description="$3"
  if ! grep -Fqx "$expected" <<< "$block"; then
    printf 'release workflow contract failed: %s\n' "$description" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

version_pr="$(job_block version-pr release-candidate)"
require_line "$version_pr" '      contents: write' 'version-pr must write the managed branch'
require_line "$version_pr" '      pull-requests: write' 'version-pr must create or update the release PR'

release_candidate="$(job_block release-candidate plan)"
require_line "$release_candidate" '          prs=$(gh api --paginate "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${GITHUB_SHA}/pulls" --jq '\''[.[] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == "main" and (.head.ref == "callisto/version-packages" or (.head.ref | test("^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$"))))] | length'\'')' 'release-candidate must accept only canonical or SHA-suffixed managed branches'

build="$(job_block build environment-policy)"
require_line "$build" '      contents: read' 'build must read the intent-bound source tree'
require_line "$build" '      attestations: write' 'build must create provenance attestations'
require_line "$build" '      id-token: write' 'build must mint the Sigstore OIDC identity'

ci_workflow=.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml
checkout_count=$(rg -n 'uses: actions/checkout@' "$ci_workflow" | wc -l)
credential_free_checkout_count=$(rg -n 'persist-credentials: false' "$ci_workflow" | wc -l)
if [[ "$checkout_count" != "$credential_free_checkout_count" ]]; then
  printf 'workflow contract failed: every Callisto CI checkout must disable persisted credentials\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi

require_line "$version_pr" '          persist-credentials: true # zizmor: ignore[artipacked] this isolated version-PR job must authenticate its managed-branch push; no artifacts are uploaded from it.' 'version-pr must document its sole retained Git credential'

if rg -U 'run: \|(?s:.*?)\$\{\{ inputs\.' .github/actions/setup-callisto/action.yml .github/actions/setup-callisto-wasm/action.yml > /dev/null; then

  exit 1

---
name: 'Setup Callisto Environment'
description: 'Sets up Rust toolchain, Cargo cache, Moon, and Callisto CLI'
inputs:
  source:
    description: 'Where to obtain Callisto: local requires this checkout; release jobs must use local.'
    required: false
    default: 'auto'
  version:
    description: 'Version tag of Callisto to install'
    required: false
    default: 'latest'

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Install Rust Toolchain & Cache
      # orin-dx/actions/setup-rust v1.1
      uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db
      with:
        components: clippy,rustfmt
        targets: wasm32-wasip1
        shared-key: "callisto-workspace-shared"
        save-if: "true"
      env:
        CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
        CARGO_REGISTRY_SPARSE: "true"

    - name: Install Moon
      # moonrepo/setup-toolchain v0
      uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095
      with:

        TAG_NAME="$INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION"

        if [[ "$SOURCE" != "auto" && "$SOURCE" != "local" ]]; then
          echo "::error::unsupported setup-callisto source '$SOURCE' (expected auto or local)"
          exit 1
        fi

        # Detect OS platform architecture for pre-built binaries
        OS_NAME=$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
        ARCH_NAME=$(uname -m)

        if [[ "$OS_NAME" == "darwin" ]]; then
          if [[ "$ARCH_NAME" == "arm64" ]]; then
            ASSET_NAME="callisto-macos-aarch64.tar.gz"
          else
            ASSET_NAME="callisto-macos-amd64.tar.gz"

## 9. GitHub Actions Orchestration (`callisto-action`)

Callisto includes a built-in composite action ([`.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml`](.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml)) that creates or updates a reviewed version PR. The repository durable workflow owns the post-merge plan, build, attestation, and protected execute stages; see [`docs/06-publishing.md`](docs/06-publishing.md).

```mermaid
%%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': {'lineColor': '#64748b', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#f8fafc', 'fontFamily': 'ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif'}}}%%
sequenceDiagram
    participant Runner as GitHub Actions Runner
    participant Verify as Job 1: verify (Mandatory CI Gate)
    participant VersionPR as Job 2: version-pr (needs: [verify])
    participant Plan as Job 3: plan
    participant Build as Job 4: build
    participant Execute as Job 5: execute (release Environment)
    participant CLI as callisto CLI
    participant GH as GitHub API (gh CLI)

    Runner->>Verify: push / workflow_dispatch
    Verify->>Verify: format · lint · test · WASM check · cargo-deny audit
    alt CI Fails
        Verify-->>Runner: Exit 1 — Job 2 cancelled
    else CI Passes
        Verify->>VersionPR: Trigger version-PR job
        VersionPR->>CLI: callisto status --check
        alt Pending Changesets
            VersionPR->>CLI: callisto version
            VersionPR->>CLI: callisto compose-pr-body
            VersionPR->>GH: Create or update managed release PR
        else Trusted release PR merge
            Plan->>CLI: callisto release plan --from-release-commit
            Plan->>Build: Intent + SHA-256 workflow artifact
            Build->>Build: Build and attest declared binaries
            Build->>Execute: Intent-bound artifacts
            Execute->>CLI: callisto release execute
        end
    end
```

### Complete Action Input Matrix

| Input | Default | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `version_command` | `"callisto version"` | Custom versioning command. Append `--refresh-lockfiles` if your workspace has interdependent Cargo/Python packages -- see below. |
| `commit_message` | `"chore(release): version packages"` | Commit message for the Version Packages PR. |
| `title` | `"chore(release): version packages"` | Pull Request title. |
| `pr_label` | `"callisto: release"` | Label automatically attached to the Version Packages PR. |
| `setup_git_user` | `"true"` | Automatically configure `git config user.name` & `user.email` bot credentials. |
| `branch` | `"main"` | Base branch for Version PRs. |
| `release_branch` | `"callisto/version-packages"` | Managed head branch for the Version PR. GitHub-token fallback branches are created automatically when needed. |
| `github_token` | `""` | Optional token for GitHub PR operations; checkout must use the same token for Git pushes. The built-in token remains the default. |
| `setup_callisto` | `"true"` | Install the Callisto environment before versioning. |
| `cwd` | `"."` | Working directory path if workspace root is nested in a subfolder. |

### Lockfile Staleness (`--refresh-lockfiles`)

`callisto version` bumps manifest versions (`Cargo.toml`, `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`) but
does not regenerate lockfiles by default. The durable release executor publishes Cargo packages
with `cargo publish --locked`, which fails if `Cargo.lock` is stale relative to the bumped `Cargo.toml` versions --
this can happen when bumping an interdependent Cargo package changes what a workspace member's
own `Cargo.lock` entry should say.

`callisto version --refresh-lockfiles` closes this gap for Cargo and Python: it runs `cargo
update --workspace` (Cargo) and, if present, `uv lock` or `poetry lock --no-update` (Python)
after bumping, before staging changes for commit (`crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs`). It is
opt-in (default `false`) since most workspaces don't need it -- override the action's
`version_command` input to `"callisto version --refresh-lockfiles"` if your workspace has
interdependent Cargo or Python packages whose versions are bumped together.

npm-family lockfiles (`package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `bun.lockb`) are not
refreshed by `--refresh-lockfiles`: unlike `cargo publish --locked`, neither `npm publish` nor
`pnpm publish` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish_client.rs`) pass any lockfile-
strictness flag, so a stale npm-family lockfile does not fail publish the way a stale
`Cargo.lock` does. This has not been a reported problem for npm/pnpm; if that changes, add the
equivalent `npm install --package-lock-only` / `pnpm install --lockfile-only` step to
`--refresh-lockfiles`'s existing Cargo/PyPI implementation rather than a separate workaround in
the Action.

## Findings that reshape the problem

1. **Spike question (a) is already answered empirically.** Release run `33679599559` on this repo (2026-09-02T20:43, head `3da710fe`) failed with the exact rejection:
   `! [remote rejected] callisto/version-packages -> callisto/version-packages (refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow '.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml' without 'workflows' permission)`.
   Raw `git push` of a regenerated branch is rejected. Only question (b), the API path, needs a spike.
2. **Live state confirms other constraints.** PR #48's head commit `e823dd73` is `verification.verified: false, reason: unsigned` (author `github-actions[bot]`). No rulesets exist on `main` or `callisto/version-packages` (`/rules/branches/...` returns `[]`). The repo allows merge, squash, and rebase merges. `callisto version` already stages its own writes via `git add`/`git rm --cached` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs` ~440-470), so the Git index after `version` is the authoritative change set. Current release payload is small: all CHANGELOGs total ~47 KB; a full plan is ~150-200 KB base64.

## Recommendations per design question

### Q1: Where to build the createCommitOnBranch payload -> (B) Rust `callisto release-pr commit-plan`

Rationale:
- Spec 014 architecture.execution says the shell "does not independently choose" anything and AC-004 forbids caller-controlled jq filtering. Deciding which paths are additions vs deletions, what to do with mode changes, renames, `.github/workflows/` paths, non-UTF-8 paths, and size limits is file-semantics policy; it belongs in typed Rust with unit tests, not in `git status --porcelain` parsing in bash (which cannot handle paths with spaces/newlines/quotes robustly).
- createCommitOnBranch cannot express modes (100755, 120000 symlink, 160000 submodule) or renames/type changes. A Rust builder can fail closed with typed miette errors; bash would silently strip the executable bit.
- Payload bytes must be read from the worktree as raw bytes (`std::fs::read`), not via `CommandRunner` whose `CommandOutput.stdout` is `String` (lossy UTF-8; see `crates/callisto-cli/src/runner.rs:39`). CRLF and binary files round-trip only if bytes are never decoded.
- Testability: pure `ReleasePrCommitPlanV1::from_changes(...)` in `callisto-model` is unit-testable; the Git observation goes through `CommandRunner` and is testable with the recording runner pattern already used in `crates/callisto-vcs/src/shell.rs` tests.
- Provider neutrality: the plan is `{baseCommit, message, additions[{path, contentsBase64}], deletions[{path}]}`; the shell does one mechanical jq mapping to GraphQL `FileChanges`. That mapping is covered by the real-binary contract test (the exact class of bug that shipped before).

Layering: plan types + builder + base64 in `callisto-model` (add `base64 = "0.22"`, MIT/Apache-2.0, already in `Cargo.lock`); raw-diff parsing and worktree reads in `callisto-vcs` (`ShellGit`, permissive); CLI wiring in `callisto-cli`.

Add a byte-fidelity invariant that makes the encoding question moot: the executor computes `local_tree=$(git write-tree)` after staging and, after createCommitOnBranch, compares it with `gh api repos/.../git/commits/<new_sha> --jq .tree.sha`. Equal tree OIDs prove the API commit is byte-identical to what Git would have committed (modes, CRLF, binary, everything). Fail before moving the real branch if they differ.

### Q2: Executor sequence and race safety

Snapshot gains `headCommit` per PR (`gh pr list --json headRefOid`) and drops `workflowDeltaFromBase` (which also removes the per-PR `git fetch` + `git diff` loop). Callisto names the staging branch in the decision so the shell never invents a branch name.

Sequence (`create-or-update-release-pr.sh`):
1. `base_commit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)`; `snapshot=$(release_pr_snapshot)`.
2. `decision=$(callisto --format json release-pr decide ...)`; branch on `kind` (noop|create|update). Read `.action.branch`, `.action.stagingBranch`, `.action.expectedHeadCommit` (update only), `.action.pullRequestNumber`.
3. Compose body (unchanged).
4. `$INPUT_VERSION_COMMAND`; `git add -A` (parity for custom version commands).
5. `callisto --format json release-pr commit-plan --base-commit "$base_commit" --message "$INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE" --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-pr-commit-plan.json"` (replaces the `git status --porcelain` emptiness check: empty plan is a typed error).
6. `local_tree=$(git write-tree)`.
7. Register `trap` that deletes the staging ref (`gh api -X DELETE .../git/refs/heads/<staging>`, tolerate 422/404 with a `::warning::`).
8. Verify #1 (`release-pr verify`) with a fresh snapshot.
9. Staging ref at base: `gh api -X PATCH .../git/refs/heads/<staging> -f sha=$base_commit -F force=true`, falling back to `POST .../git/refs` when the PATCH returns 422 (ref missing).
10. `new_sha=$(gh api graphql --input body.json --jq .data.createCommitOnBranch.commit.oid)` where `body.json` is built by jq from the plan: `expectedHeadOid: .baseCommit`, `branch: {repositoryNameWithOwner, branchName: <staging>}`, `fileChanges: {additions: [.additions[] | {path, contents: .contentsBase64}], deletions: .deletions}`.
11. `remote_tree=$(gh api .../git/commits/$new_sha --jq .tree.sha)`; require `== $local_tree`.
12. Verify #2 with a fresh snapshot (the `headCommit` field makes this the compare-and-swap surrogate for the PR head).
13. Move the real branch: update -> `PATCH .../git/refs/heads/<branch> -f sha=$new_sha -F force=true`; create -> `POST .../git/refs`, falling back to PATCH-force if it already exists (an orphan from a failed prior run; no PR exists on it by construction). Then GET the ref and require `.object.sha == $new_sha` (detects a lost race after the fact; fail loudly).
14. Verify #3, label, `gh pr create` / `gh pr edit` (unchanged).
15. Trap deletes staging branch (also runs on failure). Run to completion; report but do not fail on cleanup failure since the next run force-updates the deterministic staging name anyway.

Staging branch name: deterministic, derived by Callisto: `format!("{release_branch}--staging")`. Deterministic beats random because leftover refs from crashed runs are reclaimed rather than accumulating, and the workflow's `concurrency` group (`durable-release-${{ github.ref }}`, `cancel-in-progress: false`) already serializes runs. `managed_branch_shape` today returns `MalformedManagedBranch` for `--staging` (suffix is not 40-hex), so a PR opened from it already fails closed; add an explicit `ReleasePrDecisionError::StagingBranchPullRequest { number }` so the diagnostic is clear. Also update the `release-candidate` job regex? Not needed: `--staging` does not match `--[0-9a-f]{40}`.

Race safety honesty: REST `updateRef` has no CAS. The window between verify #2 and step 13 is milliseconds; the workflow concurrency group excludes the only automated racer; the post-move GET catches a human push in that window. That is acceptable and should be stated in the spec as the residual.

### Q3: Model changes -> remove Supersede and workflowDeltaFromBase; bump to V2 types; no runtime fallback

- Remove, do not reserve. A "fall back to supersede on 403" would make the shell branch on an HTTP status to choose an operation, which is exactly the policy-in-shell the spec forbids, and it keeps the branch-fetch/diff machinery alive for a path the spike either proves unnecessary or proves the whole plan dead. If NO-GO, nothing ships; the current code stays.
- Schema honesty: `ReleasePrSnapshotV1` is `deny_unknown_fields` and consumed by binaries that can be installed independently of the action script (`setup-callisto` with `source: auto` downloads the latest release), so field changes must be a real version bump. Introduce `ReleasePrPullRequestV2 { number, head_repository, head_branch, head_commit: CommitSha }`, `ReleasePrSnapshotV2` (schema 2), `ReleasePrActionV2 { Noop{reason}, Create{branch, staging_branch}, Update{pull_request_number, branch, expected_head_commit, staging_branch} }`, `ReleasePrDecisionV2` (schema 2), and delete the V1 types. Old action script + new binary fails closed with "unsupported release PR snapshot schema version"; new script + old binary fails the same way. Keep `#[non_exhaustive]`, `deny_unknown_fields`, the `Wire` schema-version check, and the `rename_all_fields = "camelCase"` fix.
- Keep `managed_branch_shape` accepting `canonical--<40hex>` so PR #48 stays managed and is updated in place (AC "retained replacement"). Keep the `release-candidate` regex unchanged.
- New `ReleasePrCommitPlanV1` (schema 1) with `ReleasePrFileAdditionV1 { path, contents_base64 }`, `ReleasePrFileDeletionV1 { path }`, `total_content_bytes`; input `StagedChangeV1 { path, kind: Added|Modified|Deleted|Renamed|Copied|TypeChanged|Unmerged, new_mode: Option<u32>, contents: Option<Vec<u8>> }`. Errors (new codes; E141-E148 are taken, `DIAGNOSTIC_CODE_SOURCE_FILES` in `crates/callisto-model/src/lib.rs` already scans `release_pr.rs` for uniqueness): `EmptyCommitPlan` (E149), `UnsupportedFileMode { path, mode }` (E150), `UnsupportedChangeKind { path, kind }` (E151), `CommitPlanTooLarge { bytes, limit }` (E152), `ForbiddenCommitPlanPath { path }` (E153: rejects `.github/workflows/`, `.git/`, `..`, absolute, non-UTF-8 -- the plan must never carry workflow content), `StagingBranchPullRequest { number }` (E154).

### Q4: Phase 0 spike

Where: an org-owned scratch repo (`orin-dx/callisto-relpr-spike`) so org-level token and ruleset policy match; never on this repo's live managed branch. One `workflow_dispatch` workflow with a `case` input, `permissions: contents: write, pull-requests: write`, `persist-credentials: false` (API path needs no git credentials; case A/B set the token explicitly). Setup by hand: main contains `spike.yml` + `dummy.yml`; branch `managed` cut from main with a `VERSION` file, PR opened; then push a change to `dummy.yml` on main so workflows diverge.

Cases (each records outcome to the job summary):
- A. Raw `git push --force-with-lease` of regenerated branch (control; expect rejection matching run 33679599559).
- B. `git push --force origin <main sha>:refs/heads/managed` (git-only alternative; expect rejection, cheap to confirm).
- C. Temp ref at main sha -> createCommitOnBranch(expectedHeadOid=main) with `VERSION` addition + one deletion + a CRLF file + a small PNG -> `updateRef(force)` real branch -> delete temp. Record: HTTP outcomes, PR still open, PR files list is exactly the intended files, `commit.verification.verified`, and tree OID equality vs a local `git write-tree`.
- D. Case C with a stale `expectedHeadOid` (expect `createCommitOnBranch` error -> CAS confirmed).
- E. Size probes: additions of 1, 8, 32 MiB text; record the first failure and error text.
- F. Run C twice with no workspace change to confirm idempotent re-runs do not auto-close the PR.

GO: C succeeds with default token while workflows have diverged, PR stays open and updated in place, tree OIDs equal, D errors, E limit >= 4 MiB, verified == true. NO-GO: C rejected with the workflows-permission error or the PR auto-closes -> stop; keep supersede; record the evidence in spec 013's revision note.

### Q6: Risks and edge cases
- Payload size limit unknown: measured in spike E; `MAX_COMMIT_PLAN_BYTES` constant set from the result; today's payload is ~200 KB.
- PR auto-close: never point the real branch at base; only the staging branch equals base, and it has no PR. Spike F checks reruns.
- `release-candidate` `verification.verified` check is on the merge commit on `main`, not the PR head; unaffected. Bonus: the PR head becomes GitHub-signed. Note rebase-merge would drop that signature; the existing check already requires a verified merge commit, unchanged.
- Rulesets: none today; a future rule on `callisto/version-packages` requiring linear history or blocking force pushes would break `updateRef(force)` exactly as it broke `git push --force` (Aug 6 "pre-receive hook declined" runs). Document.
- Forks: snapshot still rejects foreign head repositories; API calls target `$GITHUB_REPOSITORY` only.
- `gh` availability: already required by the current script; add an explicit `command -v gh` check with a clear error.
- Staging cleanup failure: warn, do not fail; deterministic name means the next run reclaims it.
- Idempotent reruns: create a fresh commit each run (same as today's force push); acceptable.
- `commit-plan` reads worktree bytes after `git add -A`; if a custom `version_command` leaves index and worktree divergent, the tree check catches it.
